title: fix(cli): os dev's in-place upgrade line names no origin for a refused development database
body:
Fixes #24833
Clause-②: no

Basis for the Clause-② line (the claim's, comment 6294842538): printed text of `os dev` only. No accept set, exit code, refusal, recovered boot or IPC message moves.

The seat ruled option A on the measurement in comment 6294804267: the line `os dev` prints before it upgrades a refused development database names no origin and points at the guard's own refusal. The stack half is an acceptance note (below).

## What changed

- **`packages/cli/src/commands/dev.ts`**. The coordinator's `recover` printed "This development database is still in the v17 organization-ownership shape — upgrading it in place (a copy is kept first)…" for every refusal. It now prints:

  ```text
    ⟳ The organization-ownership boot guard refused this development database (the refusal above), so os dev upgrades it in place, keeping a copy first…
  ```

  The line names no origin. `recover` runs for every `OrganizationOwnershipBootRefusal`, and the guard throws one at six places (`packages/runtime/src/organization-ownership-boot-guard.ts`: the shape read failed, the birth write failed on an empty store, and a marker that is absent, unverified, unreadable or from an older shape generation). Only the absent marker means "17.x or an 18.0 pre-release created it". The guard's own text, printed just above by the failed boot, names what it found, so it stays the one source of that wording.
- The printing moved out of the inline closure into an exported seam, `upgradeRefusedDevelopmentDatabase({ print, upgrade })`, so a unit test can drive the real line. `recover` calls it with `console.log` and the same upgrade as before. The order is unchanged: the line, then the runtime import and the upgrade, then the warnings and the verdict lines. The verdict line still carries the copy's path, from `upgradeDevelopmentDatabase`'s own result.
- One comment beside the coordinator no longer says "the v17 organization-ownership shape".
- **Changeset**: `@objectstack/cli` patch, `Clause-②: no`.

Not touched (hold-offs): the guard, its refusal text and rule; the ceremony; `utils/dev-organization-ownership-upgrade.ts` (its behaviour, its IPC message shape and its "v18" verdict line); `serve.ts`; `packages/core/**`; `packages/spec/**`; the `[schema-drift]` line (#24638's); which boots `os dev` recovers; exit codes; `content/docs/releases/`.

## End to end, on the built CLI

Fixture: a one-object define-stack scaffold; `os dev --no-watch -d file:A.db -p 0` once; the `adr-0131-organization-ownership` row deleted from `sys_migration` (tables, no marker: the guard's "absent" refusal); then `os dev` again. `NODE_ENV` unset, `bin/run.js`, `OS_TELEMETRY_DB=0`.

- `main` `19484af53` (the card's base; `packages/cli` is byte-identical at `b42c621c0`):

  ```text
  TIMESTAMP ERROR Plugin startup failed: com.objectstack.organization-ownership-boot-guard {"error":{"message":"This database carries no organization-ownership marker: 17.x or an 18.0 pre-release (18.0.0-next.*) created it, …
  [Kernel] Plugin startup failed: com.objectstack.organization-ownership-boot-guard This database carries no organization-ownership marker: … (plus 10 stack frames)

    ⟳ This development database is still in the v17 organization-ownership shape — upgrading it in place (a copy is kept first)…
    ✓ Upgraded the development database to the v18 organization ownership. The database as it was before the upgrade is copied to backups/organization-ownership-TIMESTAMP, beside the ceremony's log. The plan and the report are there too.
  ```

- This head (`0f9e4ca00d`): the same two kernel lines and frames, then

  ```text
    ⟳ The organization-ownership boot guard refused this development database (the refusal above), so os dev upgrades it in place, keeping a copy first…
    ✓ Upgraded the development database to the v18 organization ownership. The database as it was before the upgrade is copied to backups/organization-ownership-TIMESTAMP, beside the ceremony's log. The plan and the report are there too.
  ```

  The server then reached "Server is ready" and printed "✓ server started on the upgraded database", as on `main`.

## Tests

- **New pin**, `packages/cli/src/commands/dev-organization-ownership-recover.test.ts` (unit tier): drives `upgradeRefusedDevelopmentDatabase` with a fake upgrade and records each printed line. 4 cases:
  - the first line carries no "v17" and names no origin (no 17.x, 18.0, pre-release or "created");
  - it names the refusal above, `os dev`, "in place" and "copy first", and prints before the upgrade runs;
  - the warnings, then the verdict line with the copy's path, and the server boots again;
  - an upgrade that did not finish prints its `✗` lines and boots nothing.
  The sentence is not pinned verbatim.
- **Red on `main`**: the test file run against `main`'s `dev.ts` (blob `17fc74e9`, restored into the tree from `19484af53` with `git restore --source`, so not staged): 4 of 4 red, `TypeError: upgradeRefusedDevelopmentDatabase is not a function`, because `main` has no seam. Restored with `git checkout HEAD`; blob back to `3485d18c`, `git diff HEAD` empty.
- **Red with `main`'s sentence in the seam** (`node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, the anchor hit once; the replacement is `main`'s two source lines byte for byte): the anchor went from 1 to 0 and the blob from `3485d18c` to `4e8a1f86`. 2 of 4 red: `expected '  ⟳ This development database is stil…' not to match /v17/i` and `… to match /refus/i`. The other 2 stayed green. Restore: blob equals `HEAD` (`3485d18c`), `git diff HEAD` empty.
- **Green on this head**: the new pin plus `src/utils/dev-organization-ownership-upgrade.test.ts`, 2 files, 10 passed.
- **Unit subset**: every unit test that imports `commands/dev`, plus the `dev-*` utilities, `port-contract-single-source`, `console-route-ledger.conformance` and `test/vitest-tiers-partition.test.ts`: 18 files, 246 passed.
- The full `@objectstack/cli` unit project did not finish inside the 10-minute foreground cap here; it is left to CI's `Test Core`. The integration tier is left to CI as well: the diff touches no integration file and no spawn entry.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit` and `check:test-typecheck`): exit 0. The new test is in the `tsconfig.json` program (`--listFilesOnly`: 1 hit).

## Control: a bare `os serve` refusal is unchanged

`os serve objectstack.config.ts -p 0` over the same unmarked file, `OS_DATABASE_URL=file:A.db`, `NODE_ENV` unset. It exited 1 on both trees. Its whole output on `19484af53` and on this head, with timestamps and the temp directory normalised, is byte-identical: 23 lines, `diff` exit 0. That output is the kernel's ERROR line, the `[Kernel]` line with its frames, the CLI's `✗` refusal line and the boot diagnostics. `serve.ts` does not import `dev.ts`.

## Gates

All on the final head `0f9e4ca00d`, each exit code captured before any pipe.

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 67 commands from the 3 changed paths (merge base `b42c621c0`). All 67 exited 0. Two of them, `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `pnpm check:i18n-coverage`, first exited 3 (`PREREQUISITE NOT MET`: no `dist` for packages outside the CLI closure). After a full `turbo run build`, both exited 0 (`check-i18n-coverage: OK (14 config(s), 621 baselined untranslated string(s), none new)`).
- The 11 families listed under "Declared WIDE population" all exited 0: `check:init-service-contract`, `check:live-db-isolation`, `check:meta-type-normalized`, `check:optional-error-sink`, `check:resume-authority-declared`, `check:route-envelope`, `check:runner-env-posture`, `check:settings-bind-window`, `check:startup-registry-verdict`, `check:verify-stand-in` and `check:wildcard-fallthrough`.
- `--ran`: `✓ dispatch-gates --ran: 67 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 67 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero — all 67 recorded an exit code and none of them is 3).`
- `pnpm lint` (`eslint . --no-inline-config`): exit 0.
- Left to CI, not run here: the four type-check lanes, `Test Core` (the full `@objectstack/cli` unit project and the integration tier included) and `Build Core`.

## Acceptance notes

- **The stack half stays, by the seat's ruling (option A).** On an `os dev` over a refused development database, two lines still precede the new one, both from the kernel: `packages/core/src/kernel.ts:568` (`this.logger.error('Plugin startup failed: …', result.error)`; the logger writes error level straight to `process.stderr`, `packages/core/src/logger.ts:351` and `:386`) and `:571` (`console.error('[Kernel] Plugin startup failed: …', origMsg, origStack)`, with no level gate). Measured with stdout and stderr captured apart, the two lines and the 10 frames are all on stderr. `serve.ts`'s boot-quiet window replaces only `process.stdout.write`, `console.log` and `console.debug`, and its catch runs after the kernel has printed. A developer meets this once per development database: after the upgrade the marker is verified. If a puller appears, the shape is option D of comment 6294804267: a host-gated kernel change that only the `os dev` child sets, so the bare `os serve` output stays as Zone 1 ruled.
- **Bare `os serve` prints the guard's refusal three times**: the kernel's ERROR line (its JSON carries the message and the stack), the kernel's `[Kernel]` line with 10 frames, and then the CLI's own `✗` line (case C in comment 6294804267, re-measured above). Zone 1 keeps this output as it is, and the same two kernel lines are the ones in the note above.
- **The card's "#24827" case no longer reaches this path** since `19484af53`. Measured: `os migrate apply --yes` on an empty file writes the birth marker, and `os dev` over that file reaches "Server is ready" with no refusal and no upgrade.
- **Not edited, outside the surface**: the docblock of `utils/dev-organization-ownership-upgrade.ts` and a comment in `serve.ts` still say "the v17 organization-ownership shape". Neither is printed.
- **Repro fixture**: a one-object scaffold with the marker row deleted, not the card's 18.0.0-next.5 `examples/app-showcase` database. It takes the same "absent" refusal and the same `recover` branch. It has no retired column, so no `[schema-drift]` lines appear.
